Parse THETA and OMEGA parameter labels from NONMEM .mod file comments

Source: R/utils_nm.R
nm_parse_param_labels.Rd

Extracts human-readable labels from inline comments in the $THETA and $OMEGA blocks of a NONMEM control stream. Labels are used automatically as panel titles in plot_removal_metrics().

Usage

nm_parse_param_labels(mod_file)

Arguments

mod_file

Path to the NONMEM .mod file.

Value

A named list with elements thetas and omegas, each a named character vector mapping column names (e.g. "THETA1", "OMEGA.3.3") to human-readable labels. Returns list(thetas = character(0), omegas = character(0)) if no labels are found.

Labelling your .mod file for irxclean

To get readable panel titles in irxclean plots, add inline comments to the $THETA and $OMEGA blocks of your NONMEM control stream.

Format:


  ; <index>. <Label>          -- single parameter
  ; <start>-<end>. <Label>    -- range (e.g. IOV block)

The number(s) before the dot correspond to the 1-based parameter index (the same numbering NONMEM uses in the .ext file). The dot and surrounding spaces are flexible – the parser accepts ; 1. CL, ; 1.CL, and ; 1 CL.

THETA example:


$THETA
  (0, 11.5555) ; 1. CL
  (0,  9.2)    ; 2. V1
  (0,  3.1)    ; 3. KA

OMEGA example (IIV + IOV):


$OMEGA
  0.09         ; 1. IIV CL
  0.04         ; 2. IIV V1

$OMEGA BLOCK(1)
  0.03         ; 3. IOV CL
$OMEGA BLOCK(1) SAME   ; -- no label needed, auto-excluded from plots
$OMEGA BLOCK(1) SAME

Rules:

  • THETA: label every row you want named; unlabelled rows keep their default name (e.g. THETA4).

  • OMEGA: label only the first element of each unique term. BLOCK(1) SAME lines are detected automatically and always excluded from plots regardless of any comment on that line.

  • Range notation (; 3-7. IOV CL) is supported; only the first element (OMEGA.3.3) is labelled and plotted.

  • The parser is case-insensitive for the SAME keyword and tolerates varied spacing around the dash and dot.
